name: 썩은 판자 다리(떨어짐 2) (plank bridge falling 2)
label: atlas_biome_interior/plus/plank bridge falling 2
reasons: 화풍: 칸 정보량이 기준보다 훨씬 낮음 (3/4)

answer.evidence: The object is a sparse scatter of a few brown pixels (rows 4-13, max width 5) with no solid body. Several rows are gaps, and there is no top band, no front-edge line, no eave shadow, no ellipse, and no front face of 3 or more rows. It reads as flat debris on the ground seen from above, which fits a flat decal-style kind. It has no standing volume.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny cluster of broken planks, roughly 8x8 source pixels, with only 6 distinct colours. The bench reference has 14 colours and the lamp has 14, and the bench has about 5 wood steps (highlight, light, mid, dark, deep). The candidate's wood ramp shows only about 3 steps: a light plank, a mid-brown, and a dark brown. Its dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline leans brown and counts as dark_material_tone, which is good. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, but only because the piece is so small. At this size there is no visible per-plank highlight, grain or splinter detail. Next to the references it reads thinner and simpler than the bench, even allowing for a sparse prop. The tinted outline is not enough to offset the shallow shading and low colour count, so it does not meet the Beodeul bar.

answer.evidence: The drawing is a sparse cluster of a few brown pixels (max width 5, rows 4-13) scattered like fallen plank fragments. styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny brown fragment, about 10x10 px at 2x, and sits far below the references in size and craft. It has only 6 distinct colours against 11-40 for the references, which are far richer. It shows about 2-3 brown steps, with no visible grain, per-plank highlights or detail beyond a few dark and light dots. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline leans brown and reads as dark_material_tone, which is acceptable. The per-tile median of 0 means the piece is under one tile, so I judged density by eye. Even so, it looks thinner and flatter than the bench or lamp references, which carry 14 colours with several shading steps. A careful artist would not accept it next to them. It reads as a small debris sprite rather than a rich prop, so it fails on shading depth and texture.
